The test image shows a soybean stem/node with grayish-white fluffy/cottony mycelial growth at the node junction, with yellowing leaves in the background. This points strongly toward a fungal stem disease.

Top candidates: White_Mold (cottony white mycelium on stems), Charcoal_Rot (grayish stem), Phytophthora (stem lesions).
White_Mold reference shows cottony white mycelium at node junctions — very similar to the test image. Charcoal_Rot shows dry dark/gray stems — different. Let me check a couple more candidates.
Phytophthora shows dark brown stem lesions. Rhizoctonia shows reddish-brown stem lesions. Neither matches the cottony growth in the test image.

Fusarium shows dark root rot. Diaporthe shows brown stem cankers. Neither matches.

**Summary of visual evidence:**
- Affected part: stem/node junction
- Key feature: grayish-white fluffy/cottony mycelial growth concentrated at the node
- Surrounding context: yellowing, senescing leaves

**Comparison:**
- **White_Mold**: Reference top-left panel shows identical cottony white mycelium at soybean node junctions — exact match
- All other candidates (Charcoal_Rot, Phytophthora, Rhizoctonia, Fusarium, Diaporthe) show dark/brown stem lesions or root rots without cottony growth
